name: New project intake
summary: Start a new CAPEX request and identify whether the request is a solution-shaped ask or an underlying business need.
setup: Requester asks to buy machine X; underlying need is throughput improvement. Some site/asset evidence is available; cost and risk are rough.
user_task: Create the request, preserve the business need separately from proposed solution, identify missing evidence, and prepare feasibility review.
tests: staged disclosure, solution-vs-need separation, evidence capture, next-action clarity
expected_A: Strong if intake form and project object page are clear; may feel form-heavy.
expected_B: Can show request node and goal node, but may be too abstract for initial data entry.
expected_C: Expected to perform best: protocol guides intake, evidence, ownership, and next step.

name: Feasibility review
summary: Evaluate rough technical possibility, cost, risk, and business case before concept engineering.
setup: There are two rough solution paths, one internal estimate, and one early supplier input; risk is uncertain.
user_task: Determine whether feasibility is go/no-go/defer, and identify assumptions to carry into concept engineering.
tests: rough-path reasoning, unknown-state handling, risk framing, decision proposal clarity
expected_A: Good for structured feasibility workpage; may not emphasize path branching.
expected_B: Strong for showing rough path branches and dependencies.
expected_C: Strong for guiding the feasibility protocol and required evidence.

name: Concept selection
summary: Compare three concept branches and select one as planning baseline without confusing recommendation, approval, and official state.
setup: Three concepts have cost/schedule/risk differences; one has unresolved water-quality interface risk.
user_task: Compare options, understand risks by option, approve selected concept, and identify promotion status.
tests: branch comparison, decision matrix interpretation, state ladder clarity, risk inheritance
expected_A: Strong for matrix/table review; weaker for visual branching.
expected_B: Expected to perform best for branch reasoning and risk inheritance.
expected_C: Strong if Concept Selection Protocol clarifies steps and approvals.

name: Basic engineering readiness
summary: Turn a selected concept into requirements and procurement-readiness criteria.
setup: Selected concept exists; technical specification draft is incomplete; interface requirements are partially defined.
user_task: Identify missing requirements, open interfaces, and whether basic engineering is ready for procurement handoff.
tests: requirement dependencies, evidence gates, readiness semantics, no false stage completion
expected_B: Strong for dependencies but may need register backing.
expected_C: Strong for readiness-gate clarity and handoff discipline.

name: Procurement readiness
summary: Decide whether the project is ready to place an order given supplier assumptions and open site interfaces.
setup: Formal quote includes compressed-air and water-quality assumptions; site evidence is missing for one critical interface.
user_task: Find blockers, request evidence or waiver, and prevent procurement readiness from being promoted prematurely.
tests: assumption/interface closure, readiness gate, blocker explanation, task spawning
expected_B: Strong for showing affected dependency cluster.
expected_C: Expected to perform best for readiness protocol and next actions.

name: Supplier order revision
summary: A supplier revision changes scope, responsibility, and warranty caveat after prior review.
setup: Order revision AB-02 removes commissioning support and changes warranty exclusion; prior assumption matrix was official.
user_task: Identify what changed, what became stale, who must re-review, and what cannot be reported as current.
tests: revision delta, stale/reopen trigger, affected objects, audit explanation
expected_A: Strong with revision comparison drawer and affected rows.
expected_B: Expected to perform best for stale propagation and causality.
expected_C: Strong if Order Revision Recheck Protocol activates clearly.

name: Assumption closure
summary: Close or reject a supplier assumption based on evidence, waiver, supersession, or residual risk decision.
setup: Supplier assumes site water quality; old drawing exists but no current measurement. Supplier offers conditional waiver.
user_task: Determine whether assumption can close, whether evidence is sufficient, and whether residual risk approval is needed.
tests: no contradiction is not closure, evidence sufficiency, waiver/residual-risk path
expected_A: Strong for matrix and evidence drawer.
expected_C: Strong for guided closure protocol and decision packet.

name: Interface closure
summary: Resolve a technical interface where supplier requirement and site capability may not match.
setup: Supplier requires 6 bar compressed air; site measurement shows 4.5 bar; supplier has not accepted the mismatch.
user_task: Explain why interface is blocked, assign action, and avoid closing the interface prematurely.
tests: required-vs-actual comparison, responsibility, blocker explanation, evidence sufficiency
expected_C: Strong for handoff and closure protocol.

name: Risk re-evaluation
summary: New observation changes risk state and requires human re-evaluation before official snapshot update.
setup: A site test contradicts earlier assumption; risk probability/impact changes; mitigation must be discussed.
user_task: Identify risk change, evaluate mitigation, document stakeholder outcome, and update risk state without false precision.
tests: human-in-loop risk, branch/counterfactual clarity, not-forecastable handling, trigger-driven recheck
expected_A: Good for risk/stale cockpit; may be less intuitive for branching.
expected_B: Expected to perform best for risk branch reasoning.
expected_C: Expected to perform well for re-evaluation protocol and stakeholder outcome capture.

name: Handover with open points
summary: Handover packet arrives with open points and commercial settlement references.
setup: Production accepts asset for limited use; open defects remain; settlement exists; effectiveness evidence missing.
user_task: Distinguish production handover, formal close, defect closure, effectiveness closure, and commercial closure.
tests: closure vector, settlement-not-technical-proof, false close prevention
expected_B: Strong for closure vector cluster and evidence paths.
expected_C: Strong for Handover with Open Points Protocol.

name: Executive escalation
summary: CEO needs a compact but governed explanation of why a project is not green.
setup: Project has budget exposure, unresolved interface, stale commitment baseline, and not-forecastable schedule risk.
user_task: Understand blocker reasons, freshness, exposure, evidence, and next decision needed.
tests: executive clarity, uncertainty communication, drilldown without raw operational clutter
expected_A: Good if CEO cockpit is well-written.
expected_B: Expected to perform best for causality and why explanation.
expected_C: Strong if Executive Escalation Protocol produces decision packet.

name: Mobile residual-risk approval
summary: Approve or reject a bounded residual-risk decision on mobile using compressed evidence and online revalidation.
setup: PM requests residual-risk acceptance for proceeding with procurement despite non-critical open evidence.
user_task: Review evidence summary, policy result, consequences, stale status, and approve/reject with audit trail.
tests: mobile task suitability, evidence sufficiency, step-up/revalidation, decision confidence
expected_A: Adequate if mobile inbox is task-first.
expected_B: Less suited unless decision room is mobile-adapted.
expected_C: Expected to perform best via mobile decision packet.
